claims.statement: The proposed extension incorporates representations of relative positions, or distances between sequence elements, directly into Transformer self-attention.
Relative position representations can entirely replace absolute position encodings while improving translation quality on the two reported machine translation tasks.
The relative position approach improves BLEU over absolute position representations by 1.3 on WMT 2014 English-to-German and by 0.3 on WMT 2014 English-to-French.
Combining relative and absolute position representations yields no further improvement in translation quality in the reported experiments.
The proposed relative position representations are invariant to total sequence length.
The authors provide an efficient implementation of their relative position self-attention method.

The relative position method can be formulated as a special case of relation-aware self-attention over arbitrary relations between pairs of input elements, with potential application to graph-labeled inputs.
For linear sequences, edge labels encode relative position differences clipped to a maximum absolute distance k, yielding 2k + 1 distinct edge labels.
The method learns separate relative position representations wK and wV for positions from -k through k.
The authors hypothesize that precise relative position information is not useful beyond a certain distance and assert that clipping enables generalization to sequence lengths unseen during training.
Relation-aware self-attention represents pairwise relationships between input elements by modeling the input as a labeled, directed, fully connected graph.

The method learns two distinct edge representations for the output and compatibility equations without requiring additional linear transformations; these representations can be shared across attention heads, and the authors use da = dz.
The method modifies the attention output computation to propagate edge information to the sublayer output and modifies compatibility computation to account for edges.
The method incorporates edge representations by simple addition in both the output and compatibility computations, primarily to enable an efficient implementation.

Using only relative position representations instead of the baseline Transformer's sinusoidal position encodings improved English-to-German performance by 0.3 BLEU for the base configuration and 1.3 BLEU for the big configuration.

Using only relative position representations instead of sinusoidal position encodings improved English-to-French performance by 0.5 BLEU for the base configuration and 0.3 BLEU for the big configuration.

In base-model experiments without absolute position representations, evaluated on the WMT English-to-German newstest2013 development set, BLEU scores showed little variation for clipping distances k greater than or equal to 2.

The unverified Table 1 extraction lists absolute-position versus relative-position BLEU scores of 26.5 versus 26.8 for base English-to-German, 38.2 versus 38.7 for base English-to-French, 27.9 versus 29.2 for big English-to-German, and 41.2 versus 41.5 for big English-to-French, on newstest2014.

Splitting attention compatibility computation into an ordinary attention term and a relative-position term addresses the pair-dependent representations' obstruction to the standard single-matrix-multiplication computation while avoiding broadcasting relative position representations.

Tensor reshaping permits the relative-position compatibility term to be computed using n parallel multiplications of bh-by-dz and dz-by-n matrices; further reshaping permits addition to the ordinary attention term.
The same tensor-reshaping approach can be used to compute the attention output efficiently.
For the authors' machine translation experiments, the implementation reduced training steps per second by 7% while retaining the same model and batch sizes on P100 GPUs as Vaswani et al. (2017).
Sharing relative position representations across h attention heads reduces their storage complexity for a sequence of length n from O(h n^2 da) to O(n^2 da).
Relative position representations can also be shared across sequences, and the authors state that overall self-attention storage increases from O(b h n dz) to O(b h n dz + n^2 da).
The authors report that the extension improves machine translation performance.
The authors evaluate the impact of ablating the two relative position representations, aV_ij and aK_ij, associated with equations (3) and (4), respectively.
The unverified Table 2 extraction reports EN-DE BLEU scores of 12.5, 25.5, 25.8, 25.9, 25.8, 25.9, and 25.8 for clipping distances k = 0, 1, 2, 4, 16, 64, and 256, respectively.
The unverified Table 3 extraction reports EN-DE BLEU of 25.8 with both relative position representations, 25.8 with aK_ij alone, 25.3 with aV_ij alone, and 12.5 with neither representation.

The authors suggest that including relative position representations only when determining compatibility between elements may be sufficient, while explicitly stating that applicability to other tasks requires further work.
